name: The University of Melbourne
description: The University of Melbourne is a public research university founded in 1853, the oldest in Victoria and second-oldest in Australia. It is a member of the Group of Eight and uses a graduate-entry model for professional degrees such as medicine and law.
whyIncluded: Melbourne reports over 500 enrolled students from Singapore, and is a Group of Eight university on both the Singapore Medical Council and the Singapore Institute of Legal Education recognition lists.

livingCosts.summary: The University of Melbourne's own estimate for a student sharing a rented home near the Parkville campus: A$26,000-36,500 a year including rent. Melbourne gives only the rent separately, so food and personal costs are an estimated split.
livingCosts.notes: Rung B. University of Melbourne 'Your living costs' page (study.unimelb.edu.au, read 2026-10-13; no year stated, 2026 = year read), weekly cost-of-living table, row 'Sharing rented premises (with 2 others), close to Parkville', 52 weeks: weekly rent/board A$225-275, 'Estimated annual living costs (including rent/board and other expenses)' A$26,000-36,500; 'Tuition fees are not included in estimates.' Same page 'expenses at a glance': MYKI travel pass A$21.50/week. Midpoints: total 31,250 / 12 = 2,604.17 a month; housing = rent 250 x 52/12 = 1,083.33; transport = 21.50 x 52/12 = 93.17; the remaining 1,427.67 (food, utilities, phone and personal, not itemised by the university) is split food:personal 2:1 using the Australian average shares (food .22, personal .11). Other rows: single student apartment A$355-435/week (A$33,500-46,000 a year); undergraduate residential college A$24,500-37,500 a year. Replaces the earlier fallback (Home Affairs visa minimum A$29,710 a year).
